text.title: PWA Core Architecture Decision Tree
text.summary: Routes on whether offline or install is actually required, whether a native shell already owns caching and install, and whether iOS Safari is the primary target with durable-offline expectations — to the full core PWA, an install-only subset, or skip.

decision-tree.root-question: Is there a stated requirement for offline use, or for home-screen install with a standalone display mode?

conclusion.verdict: skip; a service worker adds cache-coherence risk and an update-lifecycle bug surface with no user-visible gain

branch.question: Does a native shell (Capacitor, Tauri, React Native) already own caching, storage and install for this app, or is the app hard real-time (live trading, conferencing)?

conclusion.verdict: skip; the shell already owns install and caching, and a second cache layer under real-time traffic adds staleness risk with no offline upside

branch.question: Is iOS Safari the primary target while the requirement expects offline data to survive more than 7 days of non-use, or expects Background Sync?

conclusion.verdict: apply only the installability half — explicit manifest `id`, 192/512 plus maskable icons, update prompt — and promise no durable offline data; WebKit evicts script-writable storage after 7 idle days
apply the full core: `/sw.js` at scope root with `no-cache`, immutable manifest `id`, strategy per route shape, user-initiated update reload, single registration from the bootstrap module
